about.title: About me
about.lead: I’m Eli, an early-career cybersecurity candidate from Northern Israel. I’m building toward a Blue Team role, starting from hands-on support work.
about.story1: My first technical role was Tier 1 support at Cellcom. Every call was a small investigation: check connectivity, rule out DNS, look at the Wi-Fi and the home equipment, then fix it or escalate it with clear notes. Handling a steady volume of these taught me to stay calm under time pressure and to document properly.
about.story2: Those habits are exactly what a SOC runs on, so I went deeper. I completed a Blue Team course on the SOC track at Cyber Gain Center, where I investigated security events in Splunk and QRadar, analysed traffic in Wireshark, worked with FortiGate, and practised Active Directory administration in Windows and Linux labs. I also earned the EC-Council Certified SOC Analyst (C|SA) credential.
about.story3: I’m now looking for an entry-level role in a SOC, help desk, desktop support or NOC team, where I can keep learning on real systems. Alongside security, I build websites using AI-assisted development tools.

wireshark.title: Network Traffic Investigation
wireshark.objective: Planned: follow DNS lookups, the TCP handshake and the difference between HTTP and TLS in traffic I generate in my own lab.
wireshark.environment: Two virtual machines on an isolated host-only network, one serving a test page and one capturing.

1.title: Capture traffic on the lab interface
1.detail: Interface: the host-only adapter. Traffic generated with a single HTTP request to the second VM.

2.title: Filter to one conversation
2.detail: Display filters such as dns, tcp.flags.syn == 1 and ip.addr == <lab VM>.

3.title: Follow the stream and compare HTTP with TLS
3.detail: Follow → TCP Stream, then Statistics → Conversations.

splunk.title: SOC Alert Investigation
splunk.objective: Planned: triage an alert in Splunk built from logs I generate in my own lab, from the first search to a written conclusion.
splunk.environment: Splunk Enterprise (free licence) on a lab VM, with authentication logs from my own test machines.

1.title: Ingest lab authentication logs
1.detail: Settings → Add Data, sourcetype linux_secure, index main.

2.title: Search and narrow the events
2.detail: Searches such as "Failed password" with stats count by user, src.

3.title: Build a timeline and write the conclusion
3.detail: timechart span=1m count, then a saved report.

ad.title: Active Directory Operations
ad.objective: Planned: build and administer a lab domain (users, groups, OUs and Group Policy) and note the Windows event IDs a SOC watches.
ad.environment: Windows Server evaluation VM as the domain controller for a lab domain, lab.local.

1.title: Promote a domain controller for lab.local
1.detail: Server Manager → Active Directory Domain Services → Promote.

2.title: Create OUs, users and a security group
2.detail: Active Directory Users and Computers, verified with Get-ADGroupMember.

3.title: Link a Group Policy and note the related events
3.detail: Group Policy Management, then the matching Security log event IDs.
